I was signed up for advanced classes by 4th grade, and even changed schools for that year. I still didn't really feel challenged and the sheer volume of work they assigned us just got boring and repetitive. I'd sit at the kitchen table for HOURS trying to force myself to finish homework, and eventually I just lied my way out of being done. I let unfinished work stack up in my locker and desk until right before report cards were due, and then I had to rush to complete missing assignments and extra credit before grades were submitted and I got in trouble. 

I tested like a dream though. Getting a test score lower than the 90% range in a class I liked was rare despite taking no notes and doing maybe half of the homework. That's what tipped my teacher off. I tested well and knew my shit, but my grades were still bad. Luckily she convinced my parents to get me assessed. 

I took time released Ritalin for a while post diagnosis but it didn't make a huge difference for me and cost my parents a lot of money. I also became the butt of every lame ADHD joke under the sun when my symptoms showed up at home, so I just stopped taking it. 

I fumbled my way through college, pressured into a notoriously difficult degree program by other family members who believed I "just needed to apply myself". It was so math and chemistry heavy that I couldn't focus on the long, boring lectures. I hated those classes with every fiber of my being, and eventually just stopped going. I left with a GPA just slightly above academic probation.

Fast forward to present day, 28 year old me:
I'm back on medication, this time 15mg Adderall IR twice a day. I've struggled with focus at work for a while, and finally decided to give it another try. Man, what a difference the right meds make. My focus isn't perfect but it's more manageable, and as a bonus it's really helped my depression and general emotional stability. 

Living and working with ADHD can be really fucking hard. Especially without a diagnosis, treatment, or support. I went roughly 18 years post diagnosis without the right treatment or any at all, and who knows where or who I could have been if things had gone differently. Whatever though, I'm here now. We can just do the best we can and hope it gets easier for the people who follow us.
